intro: Researchers use SEM, or structural equation modeling, because it allows them to test complex, multi-variable hypotheses that standard regression cannot handle. It provides a way to account for measurement error while analyzing both direct and indirect relationships in a single model.

blocks.text: Why do researchers use SEM for complex data

Structural equation modeling is a powerful statistical technique. It combines factor analysis and multiple regression. Researchers use SEM when they need to understand how latent constructs, like intelligence or motivation, influence observed behaviors. Unlike simple linear models, SEM handles measurement error explicitly. This makes your findings more robust. You can map out a full network of cause and effect. It is essential for social science, psychology, and advanced market research.
Common pitfalls in statistical modeling configuration

Configuring a model is where most mistakes occur. Many researchers jump straight into software without a clear plan. This leads to model misspecification. If your theoretical model does not match your data, your results are invalid. You might ignore critical assumptions like normality or homoscedasticity. These oversights are common. They often lead to biased estimates. Always check your variables before you run the final code.

items: Failing to define the Data Generating Process before coding.
Ignoring the impact of missing data points in your sample.
Overfitting the model to get a specific p-value.
Neglecting to test for multicollinearity between predictors.

blocks.text: Optimizing your research workflow on macOS

Your Mac is a capable machine for statistical work. Use apps like RStudio for heavy lifting. Keep your documentation in Notion or Obsidian. Use Zotero to manage your literature. The key is to keep your workspace clean. Use Mission Control to separate your coding environment from your writing tools. Press ⌃ ↑ to see all your open apps. Keep your analysis scripts in a dedicated folder on your iCloud Drive. This ensures you can access them from any device.
How to verify your model configuration

Before you finalize your analysis, perform a verification check. Does your model align with your research question? Are the path coefficients logical? Use diagnostic plots to check for outliers. If you use R, run summary commands to inspect your residuals. Do not trust the software output blindly. If you are unsure about a setting, ask Lazur to walk you through the documentation. Lazur can point at the specific menu items in your statistical software.
Always keep a log of your model changes. Use a version control system like Git. This helps you revert to a previous state if your model fails to converge.

faq.question: Why do researchers use SEM instead of regression?
faq.answer: SEM allows you to measure latent variables and account for measurement error, which standard regression cannot do.

faq.question: What software should I use for SEM on a Mac?
faq.answer: R with the lavaan package is the industry standard. JASP and Mplus are also popular options for Mac users.

faq.question: How can I avoid errors in my statistical model?
faq.answer: Pre-register your analysis plan, check your assumptions, and perform sensitivity analyses before finalizing your results.

causes.title: Model misspecification
causes.text: The model structure does not accurately reflect the theoretical relationships in the data.

causes.title: Lack of documentation
causes.text: Failing to record the rationale behind specific parameter choices makes verification difficult.

causes.title: Software complexity
causes.text: Statistical software often has dense, non-intuitive interfaces that hide critical settings.

fixes.title: Pre-registration
fixes.text: Document your analysis plan before you touch the data to avoid post-hoc bias.

fixes.title: Verification steps
fixes.text: Run diagnostic tests for every model iteration to identify outliers or assumption violations.

fixes.title: Modular workflow
fixes.text: Break your analysis into small, reproducible scripts rather than one giant file.
